issues: No site specific section for Newcastle in the EDI/NEW KPI meeting notes of 13/10/2026.
Region: food spend target temporarily raised to 26% until current promotions end (Matthew Jenner).
Region: hats or hairnets mandatory for all staff to prevent food contamination.
Region: menu to be redesigned with spice levels built into all ramen dishes and free chillies removed.
Region: GM and HC meeting notes must run through Google Meet so Gemini takes the notes; budget router templates updated, Monday dates must be entered correctly.
Covers fell by 206 to 1,502 week on week but rose by 145 year on year, while spend per head rose by £0.65 to £17.57 week on week but was £5.59 below last year's £23.16.
Sales were £32,401.85, down £3,220.72 (9.04%) week on week and £3,310.09 (10.21%) year on year, but £2,401.85 (8%) above the £30,000 target.

Drinks were down 1.08% (0.46% week on week) and sushi down 3.98% (2.94% week on week), while sides were up 0.41% (1% week on week), because guests coming in mainly for the £5 ramen are not adding extras and only take tap water, and there is a huge swell in students.

Deliveroo figures improved: the team maximised the 50% weekend offer with minimal mistakes and all food double checked before serving, and an unexpected 50% Deliveroo discount for the site from Friday to Sunday for the next few weeks lifted weekend trade.

Two Deliveroo refunds were requested: order 6971 for a chicken katsu curry that came without kimchi, and order 4270 involving sushi ordered with ramen, which was the site's mistake but was disputed anyway.

Labour is running on absolute minimal hours; an extra shift was not included when the figures were done, so the GM puts labour at about 22.80% (23.18% on the BOH sheet), and more staff are being sought while easing labour during the week.

Food cost was 27.22%, the highest of the nine Scotland sites and up from 24.15%, which Erin puts down to delivery platform promotions (Maki receives only 50% of that revenue), extra delivery containers and frozen ramen prep.

The GM says the stacked discounts (free ramen, £5 ramen, free sides, free drinks, free combo meal, 50% off in store, 30% to 40% Deliveroo discounts, 50% off the site's Deliveroo Friday to Sunday and free frozen ramen) make the food cost target impossible, with extra stock, takeaway equipment and soon more broth stock needed.
The site keeps running out of food when told to cut ordering, so Ka Ho has asked the GM to check in with him and will authorise extra food costs within reason.
Food variance was 0.7% and drinks variance -0.5%.
The KPI report records six 5 star and one 4 star Google reviews, fewer than usual but holding a good average, and the BOH report shows 10 reviews at 4.90 stars with none at 3 stars or below.

Weekly hygiene compliance was much stronger than the week before with no missed compliance, and pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation compliance are complete (ventilation visit on 1 October).

The kitchen sink is completely blocked, most likely because the pump macerator has broken down, so the new cooker cannot run without water and the ramen section is off sale until the technician comes on Thursday, about three to four days of lost ramen sales; Ross says a replacement macerator is needed and Ka and Ross have been informed.
Erin could not log the maintenance request and Ross says he has not received one from the site, so the GM has been told to upload the maintenance log immediately.
Other open maintenance jobs are the aircon and the relogged front door (both ultra high priority, Ross and Cheska) and the disabled lift (medium, logged).
Labour will be disrupted while no ramen is available and will be adjusted over the coming days and weeks.
Cleanliness is improving but still has a way to go, and the GM is creating an action plan for Erin to lead with BOH covering cleaning, standards, training and health and safety.

An advert is out for a new chef, a kitchen assistant is being recruited, a part time chef is sought (likely students who can work full time in the holidays), and a new FOH team member has been offered a job and should start in the last week of October.
Upcoming are all the current discounts, 50% off Deliveroo for the site Friday to Sunday, frozen ramen next week, a new broth and product later this month and Teddy's book launch.

Region: five of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites ran food cost above 25% (Maki 12, 1, 7, 3 and 8), which the Scotland BOH meeting of 13/10 linked to loyalty programme and delivery platform discounts across the group.

Region: new tonkotsu and chicken broth arrives from 15/10 and needs no added water; defrost it a day ahead and reheat it in a pot rather than straight on the heat, and a digital Brix meter is arriving to replace checking by eye, though not every site has one yet (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: the frozen ramen promotion is postponed by one week, and Penny is checking with Michael whether frozen ramen counts in food cost or separately, as some sites have already bought it (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).
The macerator pump for the Chinese gas cooker failed and filled with grease; it was repaired and fully working by the next morning's service (AM Updates 14/10).
Gross delivery sales were nearly £5,000 (AM Updates 14/10).
Michael noted Newcastle hit green twice for the first time in 13 weeks but lost £44,000 the previous month (AM Updates 14/10).

Region: Ka Ho put food cost of 25.3% to 27.2% at Maki 1, Fountainbridge, M7, M8 and M12 down to promotions lifting usage while sales projections were not adjusted; Michael said site leaders can ask for food cost and wage budget increases (AM Updates 14/10).
